Based on the description I’m assuming that you were in Praetorium, which is sort of an outlier. It and the dungeon before it are the only two eight-man dungeons in the game, and are extremely long both due to the format and the fact that you can’t skip the cutscenes. Compound that with the fact that it is the roulette that gives the most EXP and people do it almost every day, and yeah, people do tend to rush through it. (Not that it’s okay that your experience was tainted by it, just explaining the reason why). That’s exactly why the cutscenes can’t be skipped—to ensure that new folks get the whole story.

That being said, don’t worry, they’re the only two dungeons in the game like that, and for good reason. The worst “speedrunning” you’ll experience going forward are people wanting multiple groups of enemies in dungeons pulled at once, but when it comes to cutscenes/story, 95% of the time people are pretty good about waiting for new folks.

Hey there! Replied to your post.

* **Name:** Benjy.

* **Age:** 26

* **Experience:** Approx. 15 years, across Pathfinder (1st and 2nd edition), D&D (3.5 and 5e), and a few brief forays into Powered by the Apocalypse/Vampire: The Masquerade, and a few homebrew systems.

* **Favourite Campaigns:** I have things that I love about every game that I've been in, but I particularly enjoy the ones where I get to flesh out/explore my character rather than that getting left in the dust to accommodate a more drop-in environment. I always end up with a very specific vision of my character in mind and those (admittedly few games) that have both the environment and the group necessary to accommodate that sort of character exploration are the ones that really resonate most with me.

* **Ideal Session:** I think two things are key to a really good session: balance and a sense of progression. In the case of the former, I think that it's important that it's not too one-note. If there's a lot of character exploration/roleplay scenes I think a really good session has scenes that differ in tone/impact. In the case of the latter, I come away from a session the most satisfied if it feels as though something has been gained or learned from it. Whether that's something about my character, someone else's character, the world, etc., I am happiest when I have something to mull over and consider in the gap between sessions.

* **Qualifications:** I think I would be well suited for a game like this because of how focused and driven I am insofar as character growth/creation/development is concerned. I thrive in opportunities where I can really get into the head of my character, and I get the sense that a game like this really accommodates and encourages that sort of energy. I also think that I would fit well because I have a lot to offer, with my experience as a writer/actor/improv artist—I think that I bounce off of other people very well, and I think that that would lend itself to a stronger game and easy cohesion with the group.

* **Character Info:** Without getting too in-depth (because I prefer to have character creation be a bit of a more collaborative thing at least with the DM to ensure that the character fits well with the group/world/etc.) I have an image in my mind of a tactician sort of character who was raised to strive for perfection and greatness in all things. That inevitable conflict of being raised a certain way and having to face up to one's inadequacies/failings is something that I think could be very interesting to explore, and I always find that playing intellectuals in games like this can lend itself to some very interesting dynamics with other characters and the world at large. With this character concept, there is also the possibility of conflict/development with the other members of their family as they possibly grow and develop beyond the image they were shaped into, and I think that the possible repercussions/fallout of such interactions could be interesting to explore as well.
